471	function releaseFiles(dir, options) {

488	    entries.push({ name, relative });

491	  // Published release assets are flat, so every artifact is recorded by its
492	  // basename — users verify downloads with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS`
493	  // next to flat files. The CI global-artifact layout nests some files
494	  // twice; identical duplicates collapse, divergent content fails closed.
495	  const byName = new Map();
496	  for (const entry of entries) {
497	    const existing = byName.get(entry.name);
498	    if (existing === undefined) {
499	      byName.set(entry.name, entry);
500	      continue;
501	    }
502	    const existingDigest = sha256(path.join(dir, existing.relative));
503	    const duplicateDigest = sha256(path.join(dir, entry.relative));
504	    if (existingDigest !== duplicateDigest) {
505	      throw new Error(
506	        `conflicting contents for release asset ${entry.name}: ${existing.relative} vs ${entry.relative}`,
507	      );
508	    }
509	  }
510	  return [...byName.values()].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
511	}

513	function walk(dir, visitor) {
514	  if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) {
515	    return;
516	  }
517	  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
518	    const fullPath = path.join(dir, entry.name);
519	    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
520	      walk(fullPath, visitor);
521	    } else {
522	      visitor(fullPath);
523	    }
524	  }
525	}
526	
527	function parseChecksums(file) {
528	  const result = new Map();
529	  for (const line of fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8").split(/\r?\n/)) {
530	    if (!line.trim()) {
531	      continue;
532	    }
533	    const match = /^([a-f0-9]{64})\s+(.+)$/.exec(line.trim());
534	    if (!match) {
535	      throw new Error(`invalid SHA256SUMS line: ${line}`);
536	    }
537	    result.set(match[2], match[1]);
538	  }
539	  return result;

I've reviewed every changed file. My analysis:

**Mechanical refactor (the bulk of the diff):** Replacing `VerdictSurface::try_new(...).expect(...)` with `VerdictSurface::must_new(...)` consolidates the same `.expect()` call inside a helper. Behavior is identical — both panic on validation failure. No security surface change.

**`crates/deadreckon/src/commands/plan.rs`:** Changed `serde_json::to_string_pretty(...).expect(...)` to `.unwrap_or_else(|_| payload.to_string())`. This is a **fail-soft improvement**, not a regression — degrades to non-pretty JSON instead of panicking.

**`crates/deadreckon/src/commands/lifecycle.rs`:** Changes `apply_missing_codebase_error` to take `&source` instead of moving it, and `fs::read(&path)` → `fs::read(path)`. Pure borrowing tweaks, no behavior change.

**`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs`:** `normalize_goal_text` switched from `String` to `&str` parameter — pure borrowing change; BOM strip + trim semantics preserved.

**`crates/deadreckon/src/commands/chain/mod.rs`:** `chain.steps.get_mut(index).expect(...)` → `&mut chain.steps[index]`. Both panic on bad index; the index was already validated above.

**`crates/deadreckon/src/commands/inspection.rs`:** Refactored `if all || scope.is_none() { ... } else { format!(scope.expect("scope")) }` → `match scope { Some(s) if !all => format!(s), _ => "all scopes" }`. Logically equivalent — same branches produce same labels.

**`release/preflight-real.sh`:** Adds `--no-confirm` to the apply step (appropriate for CI automation; the flag is a documented non-interactive switch) and adds a `def-done` pre-step. This is a release-validation script, not user-facing.

**`release/trust/release-trust.mjs`:** Two hard-coded `*Deferred = true` flags disable:
- `publish_npm` → false (npm publishing fully disabled; no artifact published → no exposure)
- `requires_npm_provenance` → false (gated by same flag; only matters if npm publish runs)
- `requires_windows_signing` → false (Windows binaries still built, but not Authenticode-signed)

The Windows-signing decision means Windows users see SmartScreen warnings for v0.1.0 binaries and can't verify Authenticode, but the artifacts go through SHA256SUMS + GitHub attestation paths that remain enabled (`requires_attestation: officialRelease` is still true). This is a documented operator policy decision for an early release (comment explicitly explains how to re-widen). Per the review rules ("Do NOT report: missing best-practice/hardening with no concrete impact"), this is degraded verification UX, not an exploitable code-introduced vulnerability.

**`release/known-good-providers.json`:** Static manifest. No code or sink.

**`crates/deadreckon/tests/release_plan.rs`:** Test assertions updated to match the new deferred flags. No production code.

No source→sink path with an exploitable gap is introduced by this diff.
